scenarios.description: Verify the compact recording row, live captions, and capture commands.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Select a capture mode before starting a recording. Use the pen for Whiteboard or the red circle to finish. The trailing cross cancels.
prerequisites: Install the locked Desktop frontend dependencies. Use Xvfb on Linux.

runner.instructions: Run npm run test:pill from the frontend directory. Prefix with xvfb-run -a on Linux. Set APPARENT_PILL_EVIDENCE and APPARENT_LIVE_PROOF to a private evidence directory to retain screenshots.

expectedEvidence: The recording row has icon-only controls and no elapsed time. Finish and the trailing cross dispatch their original actions. Capture switches appear in the picker, and Soft Bloom and doodles appear without Labs preferences.
The row fits at 320 and 1200 DIP in both themes. The smoke checks keyboard focus, pending states, live-caption overflow, and stable layout during recording telemetry.
limits: The production Electron renderer runs with a synthetic native parent. Use the installed AppImage in an isolated VM for compositor admission and the installed macOS foreground CI scenario for child recovery during a real capture.

scenarios.description: Verify content-free nested finish spans and real bundle instrumentation without sending telemetry.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Enable Share performance metrics in Labs, finish a screen recording, and expand its Finish trace in PostHog.
prerequisites: A prepared root Rust test build. Native PostHog acceptance additionally needs an opted-in release build.

runner.instructions: Run cargo test recording_trace, cargo test workflow::performance, and cargo test demo_bundle_saves_finish_trace_without_configuration with the repository build runner. These checks do not change consent or send reports.

expectedEvidence: Worker spans retain the same trace and their actual parents and overlap, with no spans from unrelated threads or disabled collection.
A real synthetic bundle build emits selection, crop, render, write, validation and durability spans.

The whole-file English replay nests WAV preparation, model load, session creation, and recognition plus transcript assembly under the same transcription span. With the probe disabled, no benchmark span line is emitted.
The OTLP payload preserves nested IDs and exposes only bounded operation names, timestamps and a dropped-span count.
limits: Host tests do not prove native capture or PostHog ingestion. A live accepted trace must be checked against its service.version.

scenarios.description: Score recording state to independently visible and actionable Electron controls on Xvfb.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Begin a recording with the source picker skipped. The local fixture submits the recording state at the Electron parent boundary.
prerequisites: A verified unpacked Linux AppImage or a pinned Desktop frontend build with the Electron pill host and renderer.
Node 22, Xvfb with XWD framebuffer export, xauth, xdotool and the repository Bend2 toolchain on a quiet host.
expectedEvidence: Cold and warm raw latency, same-build repeat gap, observer overhead, normalized score and machine-readable traces.
Verified pixels and matching Finish action, with resource guard results.
limits: The capture state and window admission use local fixtures. Physical input, consent, native compositor admission and first media require the native Start benchmark.

scenarios.description: Score production replay finalization and verify the saved bundle on an isolated Wayland clipboard.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Finish a screen recording and copy the saved bundle. The local runner supplies the existing synthetic threshold-27 native take at the replay boundary.
prerequisites: Verified unpacked Linux AppImage, retained native threshold-27 report and its artifacts, with the default whole-file route and pinned English Parakeet model.
Node 22, Xvfb, Weston X11 backend, GNU time, FFmpeg and Bend2 on a quiet host.
expectedEvidence: Exact new bundle reference read through the packaged Wayland clipboard client, verified transcript and ink, and decoded output tracks.
Raw replay and finalizer timing, same-build repeat and probe overhead, normalized score, and CPU, RAM, storage and transcript guards.
An instrumented build retains cutoff-relative spans, observed parallel work, and unattributed time in the owned replay receipt.
limits: Replay supplies prior frames and narration. The native lane qualifies the physical Finish shortcut, real capture teardown, Desktop completion worker and finalization-window resource usage.

scenarios.description: Run calibrated Start and Stop comparisons on standard GitHub-hosted Ubuntu.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Dispatch the public repository's manual hosted benchmark gateway for record-start or record-stop with full immutable revisions.
prerequisites: Standard ubuntu-24.04 runner, Node 22.23.0, and a private artifact directory. Each Record adapter installs its own operating system dependencies.
expectedEvidence: Verified media or pixel and clipboard endpoints, same-build noise, matched control and candidate records, scoped CPU accounting, guest PSI, steal, throttling, and a qualified hosted receipt. Start also captures complete sibling-group placement and the same-subset interference proof.
limits: The hosted Start score covers the Electron pill and the hosted Stop score covers packaged replay finalization. Native physical input and real capture require separate acceptance.

scenarios.description: Compare verified recording startup or Stop-to-clipboard on two builds.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Press the physical Record shortcut to begin or finish a recording.
prerequisites: Two AppImages, a sanitized Clanker guest template, and the same verified local English model.
Four independently retained reports ordered control, candidate, candidate, control.
expectedEvidence: A focused score with baseline 100 and both paired latency changes.
Start shows the visible-pill result. Stop shows the recording CPU, RAM, transcript and clipboard evidence.
limits: Each comparison covers one Record lane. Qualification of an overall speed score requires the full journey.

scenarios.description: Save a screen recording and verify that Apparent copies a reference to the saved bundle.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Start a screen recording and stop it. Wait for the completion state and the automatic clipboard handoff.
prerequisites: A candidate build and a fresh disposable Hyprland guest with XWayland, ScreenCast/PipeWire and working H.264 decoding.
An isolated network and an operator available to approve native ScreenCast consent on the synthetic display if prompted.
expectedEvidence: The retained capture-smoke-report.json shows PASS for saved_receipt, bundle_structure, completion_state, clipboard_handoff and completion_focus for the save take.
The retained completion-clipboard.txt contains the exact bundle path from the saved receipt. The saved bundle contains the changing synthetic scene and its movie decodes.
The second take reports cancelled_receipt and cancel_idle as PASS. The outer runner verifies artifact retention and cleans up its owned guest.
limits: The scenario drives the running GUI through capture start, stop and cancel CLI commands. Picker, shortcut, capsule button and paste into another app are outside its coverage.
The clipboard and focus assertions are specific to Hyprland. Audio quality, ink and multi-display behavior require separate checks.

scenarios.description: Verify extension-free page URLs for clicks and Shift circles in the recording handoff.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Enable Recording context for agents in Labs, then click and circle a control during a screen recording.
prerequisites: An installed candidate, a disposable native desktop and two local browser pages with the same title and distinct paths.
Desktop accessibility, screen recording permission and a browser exposing page URLs to accessibility.
expectedEvidence: The clipboard and saved summary contain the matching page path at the click and circle times.
The synthetic query and fragment are absent from the full handoff, including interaction labels.
The next recording omits browser URLs after disabling the lab.
limits: The browser must publish its accessibility tree. This checks page URLs for clicks and Shift ink on the browsers and versions exercised.
